title: Layered per-vector pricing pilot with predictive batch slots and QSA intake
creator: Priya Menon
description: Run a 6-week pilot for a layered per-vector pricing model that blends a minimal per-vector floor with predictive batch slots offering progressive discounts. Primary goal: quantify net revenue per request and identify uplift in enterprise commitments versus current flat per-vector pricing. Secondary goal: surface billing system changes and security questionnaire additions required for enterprise contracts (QSA). This ticket coordinates product, pricing analytics, billing engineering, and legal for pilot rollout and contract language updates.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated revenue model comparing baseline per-vector vs layered model with representative traffic (chat + rerank) shows >=3% win in enterprise ARR potential under realistic churn assumptions
Pilot pricing UI mock in Console reviewed by Design and approved for A/B launch
Billing engineering PR for meter/batch-slot calc deployed to staging and end-to-end test passing
QSA appendix drafted for legal review including KMS options, data retention flags, and audit logging commitments
Pilot contract amendment template is created and reviewed by Sales and Legal
comments: 2026-02-10 Priya Menon: Kickoff — aligned scopes with Analytics (simulate per-vector + predictive slot model), Billing (metering schema), Legal (QSA scoping). Agreed success metric: enterprise conversion delta and no more than 10% uplift in billing overhead ops.

2026-02-12 Luca Fernandez: Data ask to Analytics posted — need time-series of per-customer per-vector usage with session length, rerank ratios, and percent of batched requests. Added spreadsheet: drive.google.com/drive/fake-simulations/LayeredPricingSim

2026-02-17 Analytics (Ana R.) comment: Ran baseline sim; heavy rerank customers show 12% spend concentration. Initial simulation of a 3-tier slot discount (0%, 15%, 30%) shows strong buyer interest in tiers 2-3 in modeled conversion, but revenue sensitivity to slot sizing is high.

2026-02-19 Design (Maya L.) attached: Console mock for selecting 'Batch slot commitment' in Billing Settings. Feedback: keep default opt-out; show projected monthly cost delta using customer's last 30-day usage.

2026-02-22 Billing (ENG-21456) update: Proposed meter changes — add 'batch_slot_id' dimension and precompute 'effective_vector_cost' in billing job. Major trade-off: increases charge detail export size; suggested compressing export and adding a rollup to monthly invoice summary.

2026-02-25 Legal (Tariq H.) note: QSA appendix must mention KMS envelope encryption, key rotation policy, and allowed-subprocessor list. Suggested contract language for audit windows and data residency options. Starting draft in Confluence: confluence.redwood/pm/embed-pricing-qsa

2026-02-28 Experiment decision log: We will run a two-arm pilot (A: baseline per-vector; B: layered per-vector + predictive slots) with randomized enterprise accounts (n=40) for 6 weeks. Chosen slot sizing heuristic: predicted 95th percentile daily burst vs commit fraction. Reason: balances cost predictability for customers and utilization for Redwood.

2026-03-01 Engineering (Luca): Billing PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1789 — includes new schema, migration script, and test vectors. Noted blocker: downstream invoice renderer needs update to summarize slot discounts; adding ENG-22491 to track that follow-up.

2026-03-02 Product (Priya): Prepared customer comms draft for Sales to pilot with committed customers. Key points: predictable unit economics, option to opt-out, early-bird pricing cap for first 90 days. Shared spreadsheet of projected customer savings for top-10 pilot customers: drive.google.com/spreadsheets/fake-projections
2026-03-02 Design review: UI ready for internal beta. Minor copy tweaks requested for tooltip explaining 'predictive slot' — Design to finalize by 2026-03-05.

2026-03-02 Legal: QSA appendix draft (v0.2) uploaded to Confluence. Next steps: Security engineering to respond to checklist (KMS integrations, audit logs, retention controls). Scheduling meeting with Security on 2026-03-05.
decisions: Run randomized two-arm pilot (baseline vs layered) with 40 enterprise customers
Slot discount tiers: 0%, 15%, 30% for increasing committed slot sizes (initial config, subject to tuning),
Default UX will be opt-out; explicit opt-in required for discounts to avoid surprise billing
Include QSA appendix in pilot contract amendments with KMS/encryption options and audit log commitments
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Billing complexity increases invoice queries and support tickets. Mitigation: Add summarized invoice line, strong pre-commit simulation tool in Console, and Sales training playbook.
Risk: Customers misunderstand predictive slot sizing leading to churn. Mitigation: conservative slot sizing heuristic and clear billing preview in UI.

Risk: Security/QSA commitments require additional engineering (KMS hooks, exportable audit logs). Mitigation: scope minimal viable QSA features for pilot and add roadmap for full implementations post-pilot.
